title: Forms and User Input
description: Learn how to create interactive forms in HTML to collect and validate user input effectively.

lessons.title: Introduction to HTML Forms
lessons.content: HTML forms are used to collect input from users. They typically contain elements like text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, and submit buttons.

lessons.title: Basic Form Structure
lessons.content:
<form action="/submit" method="post">
  <input type="text" name="username">
  <input type="submit" value="Submit">
</form>

<!-- <form> wraps input elements and defines how data is sent -->

lessons.title: Text Fields and Labels
lessons.content:
<label for="name">Name:</label>
<input type="text" id="name" name="name">

<!-- <label> improves accessibility and UX -->

lessons.title: Checkboxes and Radio Buttons
lessons.content:
<input type="checkbox" id="subscribe" name="subscribe">
<label for="subscribe">Subscribe to newsletter</label>

<input type="radio" id="male" name="gender" value="male">
<label for="male">Male</label>

<input type="radio" id="female" name="gender" value="female">
<label for="female">Female</label>

lessons.title: Select Menus and Textareas
lessons.content:
<select name="country">
  <option value="in">India</option>
  <option value="us">USA</option>
</select>

<textarea name="message" rows="4" cols="50"></textarea>

lessons.title: Form Input Types
lessons.content: HTML5 supports various input types like `email`, `number`, `url`, `date`, `range`, and `color` which provide better input validation and user experience.

lessons.title: Validation with Required and Pattern
lessons.content:
<input type="email" required>
<input type="text" pattern="[A-Za-z]{3,}" title="Minimum 3 letters">

<!-- These attributes enforce basic validation without JavaScript -->

lessons.title: Form Submission and GET vs POST
lessons.content: GET appends form data to the URL and is suitable for non-sensitive data. POST sends data in the request body, ideal for sensitive or large data transfers.

lessons.title: Fieldsets and Legends
lessons.content:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Personal Info</legend>
  <input type="text" name="fname">
  <input type="text" name="lname">
</fieldset>

<!-- Group related fields with <fieldset> and <legend> -->

lessons.title: Form Accessibility Tips
lessons.content: Use proper labels, tabindex for keyboard navigation, and ARIA roles if needed. Clear instructions and input focus handling improve usability for all users.
